task: Build the MECHANISM for a third conformance slot (SHR) in test-project001 with FB_ShredderSequencer as the block under test: stimulus head, its instance DB, the slot plumbing, and gen/test-project001/shredder-sequencer/harness-binding.json.
_manual: NO SKILL COVERS THIS STAGE. docs/15's skills cover analysis/design/build/check of PLANT blocks; standing up a conformance slot is not one of them. Done manually, to the same contract: claims before writing, mechanical gates, raw tool JSON, findings reported rather than worked around.
_lineCount: 🔴 HAND-WRITTEN HARNESS MECHANISM IR: 0 LINES. The head's index shell - networks 1-17, the index latch and clock, the six cleardown phases, the scenario, the reset request, the latched-cause check, the four published outcomes, the observation window, completion and re-arm - is 81 lines emitted by Harness.Map.StimShellGenerator. The whole of UDT_ShredderSequencerStim.ir is emitted by StimUdtGenerator (12 members derived from the rungs, 17 declared). The whole of iDB_ShredderSequencerStim.ir is emitted by InstanceDbGenerator. The FB's own Stim struct member list (29 lines) is PROJECTED from the generated UDT by the assembler, not typed. HAND-WRITTEN PLANT-MODEL IR: 126 lines - 71 of header and interface (the generator emits no header, no interface and no statics, by design) and 55 of networks 18-26. Those 9 networks are the four obligations StimShellGenerator names as the author's: the disarm lever (N18), the shared-reset arbitration (N19), the scenario timeline (N20-N23), the closed-loop contactor model (N24), the drives (N25) and the pusher assumption (N26). Every one is a claim about what the equipment does, which is the mechanism/plant-claim line, not a generator gap. Comments are the generator's fifth obligation and are authored throughout. TOTAL 236 lines.
_route: Harness.Map was called DIRECTLY through a small driver at agent-tasks/shredder-slot/gen, adapted from the pusher lane's rather than invented a second time. Not `harness-run --generate-only`: that path also runs LoopRun.Generate, which GENERATES THE COPY LAYER AND MIRROR, and emitting those from a single-slot binding would produce a mirror carrying SHR and not HBA - deleting a deployed, passing slot. Measured before switching routes: a --generate-only run against this binding was correctly REFUSED by this document's own reservedRegions ('the mirror's version region [0..1] enters reserved registers [0..1]' and four more), and a second run with the reservation stripped emitted a copy layer and mirror into a scratch directory only - NEITHER WAS EVER WRITTEN TO ir/, and both were discarded. The driver opens no socket, touches no Portal, adds nothing to harness.sln and generates only the shell, the type and the instance DB.
_files: The three generated/assembled objects. UDT_ShredderSequencerStim.ir and iDB_ShredderSequencerStim.ir carry no ir_hash because ir-hash keys CODE BLOCKS only - a TYPE and a DB report an error and a null hash - so they are listed without one, which is the documented shape. gen/test-project001/shredder-sequencer/harness-binding.json is deliberately NOT listed: it is JSON, not IR, there is no hashable-artifact class for it in this schema, and listing it would produce a 'no ir_hash recorded' failure that says nothing true. It is checked instead by the two scripts named under _selfCheck.

checks.deferred: The dispatch forbids this lane Portal, the rig and the socket - no import, no compile, no openness-cli, no download - because the coordinator serialises all of it. The authorisation granted mid-task covered `harness-run --generate-only` only, and was then itself withdrawn. NOTHING WAS COMPILED, and nothing here should be read as if it had been. THE HEAD HAS NEVER BEEN IMPORTED INTO TIA: preflight is a static filter and is explicitly not the compile gate.

_scaffoldCrossCheck: 🔴 THE SCAFFOLD IS NOW A REAL CROSS-CHECK RATHER THAN A REFUSAL, AND THIS LANE'S EARLIER CONCLUSION WAS WRONG. It first reported a bootstrap CYCLE - the scaffolder refuses without an existing head, the head is generated from a binding - and concluded the escape was that the binding is JSON rather than IR. The real escape is ORDER: the head needs only a declared spec, so write the spec, generate the head, then scaffold. With the head on disk the scoped scaffold returns exit 0, 0 REFUSALS, 21 vector targets, 23 result sources and requiredRegisters 56. The hand-authored binding declares 44 signals and 56 registers - THE SAME TOTALS - with two deliberate differences the scaffolder cannot make: it lists Stim.Start as a vector target because it does not write `startCondition` and so cannot know Start IS the start condition (a signal bound as both is refused by the copy layer), and it cannot propose iDB_MotorFwdRevSystem_Shredder.IO.FaultActive, which is outside both --scope prefixes and is this lane's boundary decision. Unscoped the scaffold returns 125 excluded rows, so the two --scope flags are load-bearing.
_generatorFindings: TWO, both reported rather than worked around. (1) StimShellGenerator S9 emits a PLAIN COIL on whatever `uutReset` names, so a head pointed at a SHARED plant reset coil is last-writer-wins against every other head - the same collision class this lane measured on DB_Input.Test[], one level down and inside generated mechanism where a head author cannot fix it. On this corpus every block's own reset input is overwritten from the single DB_Controls.FaultReset by FC_ControlMain, so EVERY multi-slot program here has a shared reset. Worked around the way the pusher lane did, by publishing Stim.ResetRequest and arbitrating in an authored rung (head N19) - which means the generator still cannot express it. (2) LoopCli exits to usage when --submission is absent, so the only production caller of these generators requires the VECTOR AUTHOR's document to generate the BLOCK AUTHOR's head - cross-party coupling the fence exists to prevent. Both are why the direct-library route exists.
_slotContention: 🔴 THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST, AND THIS HEAD IS BUILT FOR IT. DB_Input.Test[] is one shared array and DB_Controls.FaultReset one shared coil; every head writes them from Main ahead of FC_Inputs, so the last head in the sweep wins. Measured: FB_HopperBlockageStim writes Test[0,5,6,8] with NO pass-through on any, so idle it drives all four low; FB_PusherStim now passes through on all 8 of its indices (repaired by the pusher lane after this finding). This head needs Test[0,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,15] and uses `COIL DB_Input.Test[n] := Running AND <commanded> OR NOT Running AND DB_Input.Test[n]` on EVERY one, plus the same idiom on DB_Controls.FaultReset in N19. Test[15] is decisive: FB_ShredderSequencer N6 will not leave step 0 without IO.DownstreamRunning. FOUR REPAIRS REMAIN IN FB_HopperBlockageStim N21/N22 and are not this lane's to make. Tooling gap alongside it: `converter reachable-state` reports DB_Input.Test at WHOLE-ARRAY granularity, so it can neither prove index-level disjointness nor name a colliding index; the per-index picture was scanned by hand.
_selfCheck: Two scripts, and the second is the one that matters. .scratch/validate_binding.py checks the binding against the schema in src/harness/Harness.Gate/BindingDocument.cs: 44 signals, 56 mirror value registers, every key a real schema property, every resultSource carrying an inertRest with exactly one of value/excluded and a basis on every exclusion, no inertRest expressed as an IR TIME literal, startCondition not also a vectorTarget. ONE problem and it is the deliberate one: binding.unresolvedHoles, which gate 0b must refuse. .scratch/verify_head.py reads the binding's declared head spec BACK OUT OF THE EMITTED RUNGS in FB_ShredderSequencerStim.ir - watchdog, dwell, uutReset and its single-writer property, all seven phase bits and ends in order, the cause list, the outcome bits, the cycleEdges/CycleCounted correspondence, and every stim-instance signal against the GENERATED UDT's real members: 26 networks, 29 UDT members, 7 phases matched, PROBLEMS 0. It compares the document against the artifact rather than against the driver's Spec.cs, because comparing two declarations only ever proves two declarations agree.
_notVerified: Said plainly. (1) NOTHING WAS COMPILED and nothing was imported - the head has never been through TIA, and preflight is explicitly not that gate. (2) The head has never RUN: no wave, no rig, no socket, so the plant model is unexercised and the closed-loop feedback timing is reasoned from the motor block's FTTime, not observed. (3) THE CALL SITE IS NOT WIRED - FB_ShredderSequencerStim is not CALLed from Main, so as it stands it would import, compile and do nothing. This lane deliberately did not edit Main because the concurrent pusher lane is regenerating that OB through CyclicObGenerator and two lanes writing one object is the collision this project has already had twice. (4) Gate 0b, gate 5c and the map allocator have not seen the binding in its final form. (5) The register layout was not allocated; 56 is arithmetic over the declared types, corroborated by the scaffold's own requiredRegisters. (6) The pusher lane's register footprint is unknown here and unreserved.
_processNote: One self-inflicted incident, recorded because it nearly cost the deliverable. A patch script opened the binding with io.open(path, 'w') and then threw a UnicodeEncodeError on a surrogate escape - 'w' TRUNCATES BEFORE THE WRITE CAN FAIL, so the file was left at 0 bytes and had to be rebuilt from scratch. Nothing was lost because the content was reconstructible, but the pattern is a foot-gun: write to a temp and os.replace, which is what the later patches do.
